facts.fact: Custom properties are set by subscript on any ID (obj['name'] = value): strings, numbers, lists and nested dicts are accepted; id_properties_ui(name).update(min=, max=, description=) gives a number limits
A PropertyGroup registered at runtime (bpy.utils.register_class) and attached with a PointerProperty works headless; class annotations (name: bpy.props.X(...)) declare its properties
An operator registered at runtime is callable headless as bpy.ops.<bl_idname>; its bl_idname must be 'category.name' in lower case
An operator whose bl_idname is not 'category.name' is refused at registration
facts.result: ERROR Error: Registering operator class: 'BadOp', invalid bl_idname 'BadName', at position 0

facts.fact: Saved and reopened in a Blender where the classes are not registered: custom properties come back, and the registered properties' values are still in the file as ID properties (obj['bfg_settings'] holds a group), but obj.bfg_settings does not exist until the classes are registered again

Handlers fire in background mode: frame_change_post (6 calls over 3 frame_set calls and 2 render calls), depsgraph_update_post, render_post, save_post. Opening a file removes every handler not marked @persistent: after open_mainfile only the persistent frame handler still fired, and the persistent load_post ran once. (render.render with no scene camera raises 'Cannot render, no camera'.)
facts.render_without_camera: ERROR Error: Cannot render, no camera

facts.fact: bpy.app.timers do not fire while a background script runs: a timer due after 0.1 s had not fired after the script waited 1 s (timers run from Blender's event loop, which a -b script blocks)
bpy.msgbus subscriptions are not notified in a background script (notifications are sent from the event loop, like timers)
